size.note: Newman's Birds gives 24 cm, marked M.

habitat: Any well-developed woodland or riverine forest.
summary: An uncommon summer resident. The male is the yellowest oriole, yellow except for a black line through the eye to the ear coverts, black primaries and black central tail feathers, with a pink bill. That eye-line is also present in the immature, whose other plumage was not described. The female is less bright, greener above and paler below. The calls are liquid whistles, wee-er-er-wul or fee-yoo-fee-yoo-fee-yoo, longer than a Black-headed Oriole’s. Newman names no months. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Male Eurasian Golden Oriole has black wings and only black lores, a less extensive mask than the African Golden Oriole’s eye-line.
Black-headed Oriole has a black head and throat. African Golden Oriole has a yellow head with a black line through the eye.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon summer resident and names no months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. The immature is only the eye-line, and the female is only less bright, greener above and paler below, which is why this needs review. Population figures and the Kemp code NB were left unchanged.
